 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 15, 2026, 07:58:31 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th ODI: India and New Zealand lock horns in the fifth and final ODI of the series at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Sunday, November 15. The visitors hold a 2-1 advantage but have plenty to address after their disastrous performance in the fourth ODI, where Matt Henry's sensational six-wicket haul helped New Zealand bundle them out for just 89 and secure a massive 244-run victory. 
 The defeat has raised fresh concerns about India's batting, with head coach Gautam Gambhir making it clear that the team cannot simply brush aside such a collapse. With the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching, Gambhir believes the challenging New Zealand conditions provide an important opportunity to prepare for what awaits in the tournament. He also pointed out that the first 10 overs are particularly difficult for batting in these conditions. 
 India will receive a significant boost from Henry's absence. The New Zealand pacer has been released for Test preparations, along with Kyle Jamieson. India, meanwhile, will be without Gurnoor Brar, who has also joined the Test squad. Mohammed Siraj could replace Brar, while Yash Thakur is an option if India decide to alter their bowling combination. 
 New Zealand are expected to bring in Jacob Duffy and Blair Tickner as they attempt to maintain the momentum generated by their fourth ODI triumph. Will Young's return to form will also provide confidence to the hosts. 
 The weather forecast suggests clear conditions for the contest, although the pitch could once again offer assistance to the pacers. India have won the toss in all four matches so far, making the toss another interesting subplot. 
 Virat Kohli's record is also worth watching. He now shares the record for most ODI ducks by an Indian batter with Sachin Tendulkar, having been dismissed for a duck 20 times.

India lead the five-match series 2-1 despite suffering their second-heaviest defeat in ODIs in the previous game. The visitors were bowled out for 89 in 26.4 overs while chasing 334. They will need a much-improved performance against the moving ball to seal the series, while New Zealand will be aiming to draw it. 06:10 (IST) Nov 15 India vs New Zealand Live Score: Virat Kohli equals Sachin Tendulkar's unwanted ODI record Virat Kohli has equalled an unwanted Indian batting record, registering his 20th duck in ODI cricket. The former India captain now shares the record for most ODI ducks by an Indian batter with Sachin Tendulkar. Kohli's dismissal for a duck in the fourth ODI against New Zealand added another unwanted entry to his record. The statistic will be an interesting talking point heading into Sunday's series decider at Bay Oval. India were bundled out for just 89, suffering a crushing 244-run defeat after Matt Henry ripped through their batting order with a six-wicket haul. Gambhir said such a performance cannot be ignored, especially with the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching. He believes the conditions in New Zealand are among the closest India could encounter during the global tournament and wants his players to learn from the experience. India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th ODI: India will look to put their humiliating batting collapse in the fourth ODI behind them when they face New Zealand in the series-deciding fifth and final match at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. Despite leading the five-match series 2-1, India head into the contest with plenty of questions surrounding their batting after being bowled out for just 89 in the previous game, suffering a crushing 244-run defeat.
Head coach Gautam Gambhir has admitted that the collapse is a major concern, particularly with the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching. He stressed that the conditions in New Zealand offer valuable preparation for the tournament and that the team must learn to negotiate challenging periods with the bat.
India, however, will have an opportunity to bounce back against a New Zealand attack without their biggest threat from the previous match. Matt Henry, who claimed six wickets in the fourth ODI, has been released for Test preparations, along with Kyle Jamieson. India will also be without Gurnoor Brar, who has joined the Test squad.
Mohammed Siraj could return to the playing XI, while Yash Thakur is another option if India decide to make a change to their bowling combination. New Zealand could bring in Jacob Duffy and Blair Tickner to fill the gaps left by Henry and Jamieson.
With Will Young regaining form and the hosts drawing confidence from their emphatic previous victory, the decider promises an intriguing contest. India will aim to seal the series, while New Zealand will be desperate to level it on home soil.
